purpose: What is wrong with a transformer, asked once. Each case holds a status row, what the deleted ds-web `design/health.ts` answered for it (`expected_ts`, recorded by running that code once before it was deleted) and what `ds-command-kernel::design_health` answers (`expected`). A case where the two differ carries a `why`; the kernel is right in every one. `surface_divergences` records the same row as the two OTHER deleted enumerations saw it — `transformer-info.ts`'s permanent-warning scan and the register's project-wide error/warning tables — with what the one finding list says instead. Read by ds-web `src/tests/design-health-parity.test.ts` over the vendored WASM and by ds-command-kernel `tests/design_health_corpus.rs` over the native build, from byte-identical copies.

cases.note: A backend message carrying a signed URL and a bearer credential.

process_metadata.error_message: upload to https://storage.googleapis.com/b/o?X-Goog-Signature=deadbeef failed with Bearer ya29.a0AfH6SMBsecretvalue

findings.message: upload to https://storage.googleapis.com/b/o?X-Goog-Signature=deadbeef failed with Bearer ya29.a0AfH6SMBsecretvalue

cases.why: The kernel bounds and sanitises every message it emits; the deleted TypeScript sanitised only the in-flight progress line and passed error and warning text through verbatim, credentials included.

cases.note: A details entry whose count arrived as a numeric string.

surface_divergences.why: Only the register summed the detail counts, and only the register coerced a numeric string. That arithmetic is now the finding's `affected` and every surface can read it.

cases.note: A phase that reads warning without a warning block.

surface_divergences.why: The permanent-warning scan required a warning block before it would report a warning, so this row read clean on the info surface while the badge showed amber.

cases.note: The response of the run that just finished, folded in as transient findings.
A Draft error that a newer terminal Process run overwrote. The store used to rewrite the phase to `stale` and move the message to `superseded_error_message`, so health never saw it.
cases.why: CORRECTION. `normalizeSupersededLegacyPhase` (stores/design.ts) REWROTE a superseded legacy phase to `status: 'stale'` and moved `error_message` to `superseded_error_message` before health ever read the row, so the error went quiet — while `supersededPhase`'s own docstring in the same feature said "Errors are never reported as superseded — they stay loud." The supersession is an explicit output now (`design_status_row::phase_supersession`, one rule at ingest) and the retained error is a `legacy_phase_superseded` error finding. No document is mutated on the way in.

cases.note: A cached row the deleted normaliser already rewrote: the retained error is read back rather than lost with the code that wrote it.
cases.why: CORRECTION, same rule. A row cached by an older build already carries the normaliser's rewrite; the kernel reads `superseded_by`/`superseded_error_message` rather than treating the phase as a routine `stale`, so a retained error survives the deletion of the code that hid it.

cases.note: A Sketch left running when Process landed: superseded, and silent — a superseded run in flight is not news.
cases.why: The normaliser rewrote a superseded `processing` legacy phase to `stale`, which silenced it — but only because the rewrite happened in the store. A row that reached health WITHOUT passing the normaliser (the `ds design status` path, which had no normaliser at all) reported the fleet as processing forever. One rule, applied at ingest by whoever asks, answers both callers the same way: superseded and silent.
